cards.text: Friend, we're in the book of Isaiah the prophet, and right here his message breaks into a call to sing. Sing to the LORD a new song! And he is NOT just inviting the church choir.

cards.question: The prophet calls for a new song to the LORD. Where does he want the LORD's praise to come from?
The prophet calls on the people who go down to the sea, and on the islands, to join the song.

cards.text: Then the invite heads inland. The desert and its cities raise their voices, and the villages of Kedar, named for one of Ishmael's sons (Genesis 25:13), cry aloud.

cards.question: The people of Sela, a stronghold in Edom (2 Kings 14:7), are told to sing for joy. Where does the prophet want them to cry out from?

cards.text: And every one of them gets the same job: give glory to the LORD and declare His praise. Friend, that's not a choir anymore. That's a group chat with the whole planet in it, and EVERYBODY is typing.
Then the song turns, and the LORD Himself steps out. He goes forth like a mighty one, and He stirs up His zeal like a warrior.

cards.question: The LORD goes out like a warrior and shouts. What does He do over His enemies?

cards.text: Now God speaks for Himself, and He says He has kept silent from ages past, quiet and restrained. AGES, friend, and I thought MY years in the junk drawer were quiet.

cards.question: God has been quiet for ages. But now He says He will groan and gasp and pant. Like what?

cards.text: And when God moves, the land feels it. He says He will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation.

cards.question: God says He will make the rivers rise until they flood the hills.

cards.text: Then God says He will lead the blind by a way they did not know, on paths they've never walked. No map, no directions app, and they don't need one, because He's the one guiding.

cards.question: As He leads the blind, God says He will turn darkness into ___ before them, and rough places into ___ ground.
Once He has led the blind along, God says He will leave them to finish the trip alone.

cards.text: But God has words for another group too: people who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ Friend, that's like me baking a cookie and then asking the cookie to pay my bills.

cards.question: God says the people who trust in idols will end up how?

answers.text: Welcomed with joy in the islands
Left to wander in the desert

cards.text: Then God calls out: “Listen, you deaf ones; look, you blind ones, that you may see!” And His next question has a twist in it.

cards.question: God asks who is blind. Who does He name?
In the same question, God also calls His covenant partner blind.

cards.text: Then God says that though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Friend, I once stared RIGHT at an oven timer, saw every single number, and STILL burned the whole batch.

cards.question: God goes on: though your ears are open, you do not ___.

cards.text: Now the prophet takes over, and he talks about the LORD and His law. This part is good news, friend.

cards.question: For the sake of His righteousness, what was the LORD pleased to do with His law?

answers.text: Magnify it and make it glorious
Set it aside for a while

cards.text: But look at the people. They've been plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons.

cards.question: Someone steps up to rescue these trapped people and say, “Send them back!”

cards.text: No one to rescue them. I know a little about that, friend: years in a junk drawer, and every time it opened, we ALL held our breath, and it was just somebody looking for tape.

cards.question: The prophet asks who among them will pay attention to this, and who will listen and ___ from here on.

cards.text: Then the prophet asks a hard question about Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28), and his people. Who handed them over to the plunderers?

cards.question: Who does the prophet say gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers?
Why does the prophet say Jacob was given up to the plunderers?

answers.text: They would not obey His law
Their king made a bad treaty

cards.text: And notice the prophet says “we have sinned,” counting himself in. So the LORD poured out on them His furious anger and the fierceness of battle, and it enveloped them in flames.

cards.question: When the flames came, the people finally understood and took it to heart.

findings.problem: The card says the villages of Kedar are 'named for one of Ishmael's sons (Genesis 25:13).' Genesis 25:13 only lists Kedar as a son of Ishmael. Neither it nor Isaiah 42:11 says the villages are named for him, so the card states a connection the texts don't make.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The question calls Sela 'a stronghold in Edom (2 Kings 14:7).' 2 Kings 14:7 says Amaziah took Sela in battle while fighting the Edomites. It never calls Sela a stronghold, and Isaiah 42:11 doesn't link its Sela to that verse. The card adds what the cited text doesn't say.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The question tells the baker the LORD 'goes out like a warrior and shouts.' That rules out the wrong answer 'He waits in hiding,' which leaves only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says 'on paths they've never walked.' The BSB says 'unfamiliar paths' (Isaiah 42:16). 'Never walked' claims more than 'unfamiliar,' and the card isn't marked as a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The statement says God calls His covenant partner blind 'in the same question.' Isaiah 42:19 asks two separate questions. 'Who is blind like My covenant partner' is the second one, not the same question as 'Who is blind but My servant.'

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The setup says 'This part is good news, friend' just before card 7 asks what the LORD was pleased to do with His law. That steers the baker to the only positive answer and rules out 'Set it aside for a while' and 'Keep it from the nations.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card cites Isaiah 42:22 again and only repeats card 9's answer ('No one to rescue them') before a drawer joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next piece of the passage, or join card 8.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question says 'who among them will pay attention.' The BSB says 'Who among you' (Isaiah 42:23). Changing it to 'them' ties the question to the plundered people from verse 22, which narrows who is being addressed when the text leaves that open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
